alignment_evidence: The right and wrist views show the graphics-card body, but do not reliably expose its bottom PCIe contact strip and key notch. Connector orientation cannot be checked.

A PCIe-like expansion-slot structure is partially visible in the lower foreground of the right view. Its identity as the matching socket and its relationship to the held connector are not established.
The illuminated green/cyan sticks are RAM, not the target socket. The striped motherboard surfaces and card fins are heatsinks; the case rim and card support are not socket features.
The left view is obstructed by the robot and case wall. The wrist view emphasizes the card PCB, cooler and gripper rather than the connector-to-socket interface.
Neither center alignment nor keyed orientation is verified. The preceding carry provides no visual evidence that the correct socket was selected.
uncertainty: No reliable solid-surface pixel can be assigned to the held PCIe connector or a confirmed matching socket. Occlusion prevents checking the connector notch, socket key, corresponding endpoints and clearance; unobserved space must not be treated as clear.
suggested_next_observation: Obtain an oblique side view exposing the card's bottom contact edge and notch, plus a clearer overhead motherboard view exposing the candidate PCIe socket's solid housing, key and ends. Prefer a view containing both features. Any observation repositioning requires separate clearance assessment; this review does not authorize insertion or descent.
